input.body:
`executor.md` and `queue/instructions.md` are the whole stored prompt of a member's CCR routine endpoints. Both instruct the session to run commands under `<engine>/scheduler/…`, which resolves to nothing since #1326 moved the task surface out of `engine/scheduler/` into `packs/claudinite-tasks/`.

**queue/instructions.md** — the live work-item session's doc — uses `<engine>` at three sites and **never defines it**. Since #1326 no definition can be correct: no root satisfies both `<engine>/scheduler/queue/converge-item.mjs` and `<engine>/hooks/session-end-command.mjs`. Two of the three are the **terminal transition**, the step the corpus already records going wrong when a session performs it by hand instead (live on #1220, #1265: "hand-fabricating the transition instead is how an item ends up closed wearing a live status").

**executor.md** defines `<engine>` as "the parent of the directory this file sits in (this file is `<engine>/scheduler/executor.md`)". The file sits at `packs/claudinite-tasks/executor.md`, so `<engine>` is `packs/` and its commands resolve to `packs/scheduler/resolve-dispatch.mjs`, `packs/scheduler/record-exec.mjs`, `packs/hooks/session-end-command.mjs` — none exist, in the canon or in a mount. This doc is the **retired** slot mechanism's, kept for routines not yet repointed, so it is the narrower half of the blast radius.

`git log --follow` shows `a248483` copied both docs `C100` from `engine/scheduler/`. That commit rewrote the stubs' `run:` lines and left the prose naming the old root. No test asserts the command paths; `test/legacy-protocol.mjs` pins `engine/scheduler/…` only as tolerated *input* (a stale member's issue body), not as a command target.

**Fix.** Stop the docs naming a root they cannot derive. Define the base as the directory the file sits in and address everything relative to it — correct in the canon home and in a mount, and stable across any future relocation of the pack's internals.

**Assurance.** A `runnable-doc-commands` check asserting every `node <path>` in a pack's operational Markdown resolves to a file in the tree. Nothing opens a path written in prose until an agent follows it, which is why this sat broken for two months.

input.title: Re-shelve claudinite-tasks by stage: src/ for the code, queue/ frozen as workflow ABI
input.body:
`packs/claudinite-tasks/` carries ~24 modules at its root. That is sediment, not design: `git log --follow` on any of them shows one event — `a248483` (#1326) copied the whole flat `engine/scheduler/` directory in with `C100`. The pack root *is* the old flat scheduler dir, and `queue/` is the one sub-system that had already been carved out inside it before the move.

## The stages are already separable

An import graph over the pack (tests excluded) collapses to five stages with **exactly one** backward edge:

| Stage | Cross-stage edges |
|---|---|
| schedule — `scheduler-run`, `readiness`, `schedule-board`, `create-work-item`, `tick`, `drain-dispatch` | ⚠️ one: `queue/scheduler-run.mjs:32` imports `pickOrder` from `queue/executor.mjs` |
| execute-code — `code-work`, `code-work-run`, `prework-run`, `secrets-bag` | none |
| execute-agent — `resolve-dispatch`, `validate-dispatch`, `invoke`, `executor-continuation` | none |
| finalize — `converge-item`, `verify-outcome`, `record-exec`, `land-pr`, `deliver-generated` | none (invoked as CLI from prose, never imported by the executor) |
| recover — `janitor-rules`, `workflow-failure`, `task-janitor` | none |

That edge is placement, not coupling. `queue/executor.mjs` (672 lines) hosts two functions that are not executor mechanics: `pickOrder` (ordering policy over the queue, called by the scheduler run) and `evaluatePrecondition` (the contract's evaluator, published through `shared-code/task-contract.mjs` and re-run by both sides). Extract those two and the DAG is strictly one-directional — at which point the `barriers` pack can enforce it pointed inward, with no bespoke check.

The kernel is small and falls out of fan-in: `queue/work-item.mjs` (14 importers), `merge-policy.mjs` (6), `calendar.mjs` / `task-contract.mjs` / `queue/anchors.mjs` (5 each), `run-record.mjs` (4), `queue/leases.mjs` (3).

## What cannot move

Two of these cannot be repaired by a converge, and they shape the whole layout:

1. **Workflow `run:` targets** — stamped into every member's `.github/workflows/` at adoption, the one directory a converge may never push to. Five frozen paths: `queue/scheduler-run.mjs`, `queue/drain-dispatch.mjs`, `queue/workflow-failure.mjs`, `queue/executor.mjs`, `queue/executor-continuation.mjs`. Moving one costs a human-merged PR per member.
2. **`executor.md` and `queue/instructions.md`** — CCR routine endpoints, a per-repo console setting (`adopt-pack` §4b). Moving one needs every member re-pointed by hand.
3. Engine-mandated names: `pack.mjs`, `worldRules/`, `workRules/`, `tasks/`, `skills/`, `migrations/` and the metadata files.

So `queue/` survives as exactly **five one-line re-export shims plus `instructions.md`**, with a header saying it is workflow ABI and may never hold logic again. Everything else internal goes under `src/`.

## `shared-code/` → `src/contract/`, with shims

The barrier's allow list names `packs/claudinite-tasks/shared-code` as the one path another pack may import (`.claudinite/local/packs/canon-curation/declared-checks.json`). The nine modules there are all `export *` — 52 lines total — so they curate nothing today; their whole value is being a stable address. `contract` names that better, and absorbs the existing `task-contract` sense rather than colliding with it: what a task must declare, and what another pack may import.

**It needs shims.** `planPackUpdates` (`packs/claudinite-lifecycle/updates/pack-update.mjs:76`) marks a pack `blocked` when its `minEngineVersion` exceeds the member's engine — **that pack alone is held back while its siblings land**. So a member can hold a new `claudinite-dashboard` beside a blocked `claudinite-tasks`; if the dashboard imports `src/contract/…` and the mount carries only `shared-code/`, that pack fails to load, the mount fails its self-test, the converge refuses to land at all, and the member cannot receive the version that would fix it. That is the #1004 class exactly. So: move the modules, leave `shared-code/*` re-exporting, retire them on a stamp-confirmable precondition — "no member's `packVersions['claudinite-tasks']` predates the rename" — never a date.

Reference inventory: 15 non-test import sites across 5 consumer packs (dashboard ×5, fleet-sheepdog, basics, growth, lifecycle), 17 in tests, 13 prose/config mentions, the barrier's allow-list string (which must name both paths during the window), and one cross-pack path reference in `claudinite-dashboard/test/pack.test.mjs` reading `claudinite-tasks/stubs/…`.

## Target layout

```
packs/claudinite-tasks/
  pack.mjs  README.md  VERSIONS.md  badge.svg
  executor.md                          ← frozen (console routine)
  worldRules/  workRules/  tasks/  migrations/     ← engine-mandated

  queue/                               ← FROZEN WORKFLOW ABI, nothing else ever
    scheduler-run.mjs  drain-dispatch.mjs  workflow-failure.mjs
    executor.mjs  executor-continuation.mjs        (5 one-line re-exports)
    instructions.md                    ← frozen (console routine)

  src/
    contract/    work-items  anchors  task-contract  merge-policy  signals
                 github  delivery  usage-format  wake          (barrier-allowed)
    model/       work-item  leases  calendar  anchors  task-contract
                 precondition ←extracted  merge-policy  model-map  run-record
                 built-in-tasks  discover  dispatch
    gh/          read  write  tracker  read-items
    signals/     collectors + for-task
    schedule/    run  readiness  schedule-board  create-work-item  tick
                 drain-dispatch  pick-order ←extracted
    execute/     loop  apply-status  heartbeat  suspend
      code/      code-work  run  prework-run  secrets-bag
      agent/     resolve-dispatch  validate-dispatch  invoke  continuation
      built-in/implement-request/   (NOT tasks/ — engine-owned, registered separately)
    finalize/    converge-item  verify-outcome  record-exec  land-pr
                 deliver-generated  narrow-diff  deliver-pr.md
    recover/     janitor-rules  workflow-failure
    adopt/       converge-workflows  hash-minute  stubs/

  shared-code/   ← 9 re-export shims → src/contract/, retired on the stamp
  test/          mirrors src/
```

**The invariant:** `src/model/` and `src/gh/` import nothing from a stage; stages import only downward; no stage imports another stage; `src/contract/` only re-exports.

## Also in scope

- `run.mjs` and `slots.mjs` at the pack root are shims for the retired slot scheduler. Nothing in the tree imports either, and `engine-pack-lane-shims.test.mjs` guards `engine/**` paths, not these — confirm against fielded history, then delete rather than relocate.
- `README.md` claims `engine/scheduler/*` still exists as shims. It does not; `engine/` has had no `scheduler` directory since #1326.

Roughly 60 module moves and 50 test moves. The sweep mechanics (`repo-text-sweeps`) matter more than the volume; #1475 lands first and independently, since correcting the docs' base is what stops this move from orphaning their commands a second time.

---
name: merge-to-main
description: Merge the change in front of the owner into main. Use when the owner says "LGTM" or asks to merge/land the current branch or PR into main.
---

# Merge to main

If the project's own `CLAUDE.md` names a merge-policy file, that file overrides the divergent
points below (merge method, CI gating). Don't go hunting for one it doesn't name.

1. Load `create_pull_request` + `merge_pull_request` in one `ToolSearch`.
2. No PR open for the branch? `create_pull_request` (base `main`), body ending `Closes #<issue>`.
3. If the PR has check runs, wait for them to pass. None — merge without waiting.
4. `merge_pull_request`, `merge_method: squash`, title `<subject> (#<pr>)`. Don't pre-read
   mergeability; the call fails loudly.
5. Sync local `main`: `git checkout main && git pull origin main`.
6. Capture the conversation:
   `node .claudinite/shared/packs/claudinite-growth/capture-log.mjs --issue <n>`
   (in the canon repo: `node packs/claudinite-growth/capture-log.mjs --issue <n>`). Skip only if
   the repo doesn't declare `claudinite-growth`. A later merge in the same session runs it again.
7. Run the basics pack's
   [verify-in-production](../../../basics/skills/verify-in-production/SKILL.md) skill, unasked.
   This step is that skill's **only** trigger — it files against what the squash actually landed,
   which is why it runs here and not when the code was written or the PR opened. It decides
   whether this change needs a production check at all — most don't — and files the issue that
   comes back once the change is live. Never offer the owner to check later instead.

Don't re-read the issue to confirm it closed — `Closes #<issue>` does that on merge.

with:
          node-version: 20
      - name: Unit tests
        # THE test roots — a closed set of FOLDERS, each swept to any depth. Depth is
        # deliberately not enumerated: the previous form spelled out one glob per level of
        # nesting, so a test at an unlisted depth was silently never run — which is exactly
        # how vendoring/'s two files sat outside CI. `**` removes depth from the question;
        # what remains is the root list, and engine-tests/ci-test-roots.test.mjs fails the
        # moment a tracked test lands outside it. Adding a root is a deliberate CI edit;
        # adding a test is not.
        #   engine-tests/            engine/ (migrations included) + the other top-level canon code;
        #                            mirrors engine/'s inner structure, and stays canon-side
        #                            because engine/ ships to consumers exactly as-is (#385)
        #   packs/                   every canon pack's tests, each inside the pack it covers
        #   vendoring/               co-located with the vendor computer/writer they cover,
        #                            the fixture-consumer rehearsal included
        #   dev/tools/               maintainer-side tooling nothing at session time runs
        #   .claudinite/local/packs/ this repo's own local packs — tests live inside the tree
        # nullglob: a root with no tests drops out instead of reaching node as a literal pattern.
        run: |
          shopt -s globstar nullglob
          tests=(engine-tests/**/*.test.mjs packs/**/*.test.mjs vendoring/**/*.test.mjs dev/tools/**/*.test.mjs .claudinite/local/packs/**/*.test.mjs)
          # Deliberately oversubscribed. node --test defaults to one worker per core
          # minus one, which fits a CPU-bound suite; this one spends most of its wall
          # clock waiting — on git plumbing, spawned workers and converge fixtures — so
          # the cores idle at that default (measured on this tree: 106s wall against
          # 187s of user+sys on 4 cores). Doubling the workers: 106s -> 70s, with 16
          # buying only another 2s.
          #
          # TAP goes to a FILE, not the log. 2,448 tests emit ~13,000 lines at 5.3
          # lines each, and a failing run's one `not ok` sits wherever its file
          # finished — while GitHub's job-log API serves only a TAIL and the signed
          # blob URL that would serve the whole thing is proxy-blocked. So a red run
          # said `# fail 1` and nothing more, and five green local re-runs could not
          # name the test (#1170). Printing the failing blocks puts the identity in
          # the tail, where it can actually be read.
          status=0
          node --test --test-concurrency=$(( $(nproc) * 2 )) "${tests[@]}" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/tests.tap" || status=$?
          if [ "$status" -ne 0 ]; then
            echo '::group::failing tests'
            grep -n -A 25 '^not ok' "$RUNNER_TEMP/tests.tap" || echo 'no `not ok` line — the runner died before reporting one'
            echo '::endgroup::'
          fi
          tail -n 12 "$RUNNER_TEMP/tests.tap"
          exit "$status"
      - name: Conformance sweep (world scope)
        # The tree as it stands — the pattern bootstrap wires into consumers.
        run: node engine/checks/check_the_world.mjs
      - name: Conformance sweep (work scope)
        # The CHANGE, not the tree: this branch's diff against the base branch, the
        # only scope that can see what a commit did rather than what the repo now
